findings.C00-R1: A path is one canonical repository-relative identity: separators, dot segments and letter case do not make a second path, and escaping, absolute, drive, stream, reserved-device and short-name spellings are refused. Claims overlap when one identity equals or contains the other. Exclusion is ordered: each attempt is hard-linked under the next free dense sequence number and yields to every earlier overlapping attempt that won or has not decided, so overlapping attempts cannot both win. Hot-file checks use the same identity and fail closed.
findings.C00-R2: A handoff is a record the integrator issues to one exact process identity, node, base and canonical scope. An id alone, a mismatch, a non-integrator issuer or a second use is refused as handoff-invalid. A valid handoff does not displace a live claim and is used only by a winning claim.
findings.C00-R3: An owner is role, host, pid, process start instant and worktree, compared after respelling. Claim release, slot release and work mode all use it; the integrator may end another holder's claim only with a recorded reason. The command line requires --pid and reads that process's start time from the operating system unless --start is given.
findings.C00-R4: A profile model says runtime exactly when it names a reported model, as directOrigin records it, and saved-run compatibility skips contradictory step records. Authoritative run ids, event run ids and continuation ofRunId use the run store's identifier pattern, copied byte-identically and parity-tested. The first round left forkPoint a bounded id, wrongly saying no step-id pattern existed; the second round gives it the run service's step id pattern (see second_round.findings.F3).
findings.C00-R5: This record no longer hashes itself or its patch; the outer manifest does, over Git blob bytes. The stale 30/30 text, the 38 proposed-new anchor text, HAR-10 and AGENTS.md frozen wording and the cp1252 bytes in dependency-order.md are corrected, and site anchors are bound to the site repository.

findings.F1: The earlier tool on the shared root defeats exclusion. Fixed where the repaired tool was at fault: an ordered claim ends only by a release from its holder or from the integrator with a reason, a release record without that authority is ignored, and the authoritative release is then recorded as claims/releases/<id>.json; a claim the earlier tool writes while an attempt waits is read again just before the attempt can win. The earlier tool's own blindness to aliases, directories and ordered attempts is the rollout requirement in blockers.
findings.F2: A retried unslot removed the next holder's slot. A slot is now released once: slot/releases/<slotId>.json is published exclusively before heavy.json is removed, and a release that finds the record removes nothing.
findings.F3: forkPoint accepted ids the runtime refuses and rewrote padded ones. STEP_ID_PATTERN copies STEP_ID from server/harness/run-service.ts byte-identically, forkPoint uses it without trimming, and the test compares it with RunService.step.
findings.E1: A path whose lock file name exceeds 255 characters threw after the claim won. It is now refused as invalid before anything is published.
findings.E2: Work mode ignored undecided attempts. It is now read-only while another process has an overlapping attempt that has not decided.
findings.E3: The handoff was used before the decision, so an attempt ended while it waited used it up. Only a winning claim now uses its handoff, and a claim that wins after another claim used the same handoff gives its paths back.
